reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing over-flagged.

The cited text (Section 8.3) fixes a definite termination trigger (last Receivable paid/settled/sold/written off, or termination of the Issuer under the Trust Agreement) with no automatic renewal term, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price-uplift mechanic, so none of the evergreen risks RENEWAL targets arise.

Absence of auto-renewal is at least as protective as the preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement); classifying as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct because the rule's risk (hard-to-exit evergreen terms) cannot materialize here.
The failed deterministic check ('notice window number not found') is explained by the genuine absence of any renewal notice mechanic, not by a phrasing miss, so it does not undercut the finding.
Rationale is accurate and appropriately notes that grafting an opt-out/CPI-cap construct onto a securitization transfer and servicing agreement would be structurally inapposite.
